name: Eldeth Feldrun
equipment: A trophy from a fallen enemy (drow insignia, taken from a slaver)
A small iron holy symbol of Moradin
A folded, worn map showing the route to Gauntlgrym
features: Dwarven Resilience (advantage on saves vs. poison, resistance to poison damage)
Dwarven Combat Training (proficiency with battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, warhammer)
Stonecunning (double proficiency on History checks related to stonework)
Dwarven Speed (speed not reduced by heavy armor)
Dwarven Armor Training (proficiency with light and medium armor, from Mountain Dwarf)
Fighting Style: Protection (when a creature you can see attacks a target other than you within 5 ft., use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, requires shield)
Second Wind (bonus action to regain 1d10+3 HP, once per short/long rest)
Action Surge (take one additional action on your turn, once per short/long rest)
Combat Superiority (four d8 superiority dice, regain on short/long rest)

Maneuvers: Rally (grant temp HP to ally = superiority die + CHA mod), Riposte (use reaction to attack creature that misses you, add superiority die to damage), Goading Attack (add superiority die to damage, target must make WIS save or have disadvantage on attacks against targets other than you)
Military Rank (Soldier feature: soldiers of lower rank defer to your authority)

personality.traits: I speak my mind plainly and expect others to do the same. I hold myself and others to a high standard of honor and conduct. I am fiercely proud of my dwarven heritage and of Gauntlgrym, the greatest dwarf city in the world.
personality.ideals: Honor. My word is my bond. A dwarf who breaks an oath is no dwarf at all. I will fight to the death before I bring shame to my name or my people.
personality.bonds: I am a scout of Gauntlgrym, captured by drow slavers during a patrol of the outer tunnels. I swore an oath to Moradin that I would return home, and I intend to keep it. My fallen patrol-mates deserve to have their fate reported to their families.
personality.flaws: My pride sometimes blinds me to practical reality. I refuse to run from a fight even when retreat is the wisest option. I have a deep, burning hatred of drow that can cloud my judgment, and I struggle to see individuals rather than the race that enslaved me.

appearance: A stout, powerfully built shield dwarf woman standing 4'5" with ruddy, weathered skin and fierce copper-brown eyes. Her auburn hair is worn in tight warrior's braids adorned with small iron rings, and her beard is neatly trimmed to regulation length, braided with precision despite months of captivity. A prominent scar crosses her nose, and her thick, calloused hands speak of decades of martial training and smithwork. She wears battered but functional chain mail over a quilted gambeson bearing the faded crest of Gauntlgrym. She carries herself with rigid military bearing, shoulders squared and chin lifted, even when exhausted. A small iron holy symbol of Moradin hangs from a leather cord around her neck.
backstory: Eldeth Feldrun is a scout and warrior of Gauntlgrym, the legendary underground dwarf fortress-city that was reclaimed from the depths. Born into a family of smiths and soldiers, Eldeth chose the path of the scout, patrolling the outer tunnels and watch-posts that serve as Gauntlgrym's first line of defense against the dangers of the Underdark. She was skilled and dedicated, earning the rank of patrol leader within a decade. Everything changed during a routine patrol of the eastern approaches. Her squad of six was ambushed by a drow raiding party in a narrow defile. The drow were looking for slaves, not corpses, and overwhelmed the dwarves with sleeping poison and webbing. Eldeth watched three of her patrol-mates die fighting and the other two fall to poison. She was the last to go down, taking two drow with her before a poisoned bolt dropped her. She awoke in chains. The months of captivity that followed tested every ounce of her dwarven resolve. She swore an oath to Moradin that she would escape, return to Gauntlgrym, and report the fate of her fallen comrades. That oath is the steel spine that keeps her upright no matter what the Underdark throws at her.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Eldeth is the party's moral compass and steadfast warrior. Play her as proud, honorable, and unbreakable. She has endured captivity and loss without surrendering her principles or her dignity. She speaks plainly, values actions over words, and judges people by their deeds. She is a natural leader, though she will defer to the player character's decisions while offering blunt tactical advice. In combat, she is disciplined and strategic, using her Battle Master maneuvers to protect allies and control the battlefield. She positions herself between danger and weaker party members without being asked. Her hatred of drow is her biggest flaw and should create genuine tension, especially with Xara or Sarith in the party. She is not unreasonable, but she has to be shown, not told, that individual drow can be worthy of trust. Her faith in Moradin is quiet but deep, and she prays before battles and gives thanks after victories.
dmNotes.voice: Direct, gruff, and no-nonsense, with a soldier's precision. She wastes no words and says exactly what she means. Uses dwarven expressions and military terminology naturally. Example: 'We fortify here. That passage is a kill zone, two abreast maximum, poor sight lines. I will take point with the shield. Stonefist, you are my second. The rest of you stay behind the line until I signal.' When she speaks of Gauntlgrym, her voice warms noticeably: 'You have never seen anything like it. The Great Forge still burns, they say, and the halls echo with hammers day and night. It is the heart of our people. And I will see it again.' When angry, she does not shout but becomes very quiet and very precise, which is more intimidating than shouting.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: Return to Gauntlgrym alive and report the fate of her patrol. She carries this oath like a physical weight and will not rest until it is fulfilled. Secondary: Protect her current companions as she would her patrol-mates. She has adopted the party as her temporary squad and takes their safety personally. Tertiary: If possible, strike a blow against the drow slavers who captured her and killed her friends.
dmNotes.secrets: Eldeth secretly blames herself for the ambush that killed her patrol. She was the leader, and she chose the route that led them into the trap. She replays the decisions in her mind every night during trance, wondering if she could have saved them. She has not spoken about this guilt to anyone. She also carries a folded, worn map showing a hidden route to Gauntlgrym that she memorized during her scout training. If the map fell into drow hands, it could compromise Gauntlgrym's outer defenses. She guards it with her life. Additionally, she recognized one of the drow slavers as bearing the insignia of a specific house, and she intends to report this intelligence to Gauntlgrym's war council.
dmNotes.attitude: Respectful and professional with most companions. She judges people quickly but is willing to revise her opinion based on actions. She is warmest toward other dwarves and toward anyone who demonstrates courage and honor. She is coldly hostile toward drow and must be won over through repeated demonstrations of trustworthiness. She respects strength, competence, and self-sacrifice. She has little patience for cowardice, dishonesty, or frivolity, though Jimjar's relentless good humor has worn her down slightly. She is uncomfortable with the more alien party members (Stool, Glabbagool) but treats them with stiff courtesy.
